question: Saving an organization integration returns "organization admin only" or "no organization is associated with your account". What now?
answer:
Two different server-side refusals on /api/org-connections, so they apply from any client:

• "organization admin only" (403) — your role is not org_admin (or owner). Members and site managers cannot set organization-wide credentials. Ask your organization admin; they set it once and every member's scans use it.

• "no organization is associated with your account" (400) — your role passed, but your account has no organization_id. This is the platform-owner case: an owner sits above organizations and belongs to none. Use an org-admin account inside the organization you want to configure. It is also why the "Organization integrations" panel is hidden for the owner.
symptoms: no organization is associated with your account
rootCause: requireOrgAdmin in connection_profiles_routes.js returns 403 for roles outside org_admin/owner and 400 when req.user.organization_id is missing, which is the platform owner's case; OrgConsolePage hides the panel for owners.

question: How do I stop using a data source, or delete one? Is there an off switch?
answer:
No off switch — the Data Sources screen only offers switch or delete.

Switch: press "Use" on another saved connection. The previous one stops being active immediately and stays saved.

Delete: tap the ⋯ menu on the card → "Delete" → confirm `Delete connection "<name>"?`. This is permanent; the stored credentials live in the same row and are destroyed with it, so you would have to re-enter them.

If you delete the active connection and have no other, the screen shows "No active connection." with the hint "Add a connection below to start pulling data from your CMDB", and CMDB-backed screens return nothing until you add one.

(Organization-wide credentials use the "Remove" button in Organization integrations instead.)
symptoms: How do I disconnect a data source
How do I turn off a connection without deleting it
rootCause: ConnectionsPage exposes only Edit and Delete in the card menu plus the Use button; the /api/connections/deactivate route exists but no control on the page calls it, and remove() deletes the row (secret blob included).

evidence.snippet:
No active connection.

Add a connection below to start pulling data from your CMDB.

question: INTERNAL: how are connection-profile credentials stored, and what may I say about it to a customer?
answer:
INTERNAL — storage model (do not paste to customers):
• Connection-profile credentials (personal and org-wide) are serialised to JSON and sealed with AES-256-GCM before they reach the database. The row stores base64(iv|tag|ciphertext) in connection_profiles.secret_blob. Only user_id, name, type, is_active, organization_id and timestamps are in cleartext.
• Key: 32 bytes as 64 hex chars, from SSH_CREDS_KEY if set, else server/.env.key (generated 0600 on first run). Same key as the SSH credential store — one rotation surface.
• Decryption happens only inside the server process, in resolveCredsForOrg / resolveCredsForType, at the moment an outbound call is made. Nothing decrypts on the client.
• No route returns plaintext. Create, update, list, get and activate all reply through rowToMeta/orgRowToMeta — metadata only, including for the admin who set an org credential.

Handling rules:
• Never read out, copy, screenshot, relay or "confirm" a stored secret — to anyone, including the account owner or an org admin. There is no supported way to retrieve one; do not invent one.
• Never ask a customer to send a password, token or connection string in a ticket. If a credential must change, they re-enter it themselves in the app.
• Do not discuss key file paths, env var names or database column names with customers.

Safe customer-facing phrasing: "Your credentials are encrypted before they're stored and are never shown again — not even to you. To change one, just re-enter it."
symptoms: Customer asks us to retrieve their stored password
rootCause: connection_profiles.js encrypts the secret JSON with the shared AES-256-GCM helper from ssh-creds.js and persists only the blob; all HTTP responses go through rowToMeta/orgRowToMeta, which omit secret_blob.

evidence.snippet:
* One row per saved connection. The actual credentials (instance URL,
 * username, password, API tokens, optional vendor-specific extras) live
 * in an AES-256-GCM blob; only metadata (name, type, created_at, etc.)
 * is queryable in cleartext.
...
 * Encryption key is shared with the SSH creds store — same AES key file
 * (server/.env.key) or SSH_CREDS_KEY env var. One key, one rotation
 * surface.

question: INTERNAL: every connection suddenly stopped working after a server change and the log shows decrypt failures. What happened?
answer:
The AES key no longer matches the stored blobs. Both stores (connection profiles and SSH creds) share one key: SSH_CREDS_KEY env var, else server/.env.key.

What you see:
• "[connection_profiles] decrypt failed for profile <id>" or "[connection_profiles] org decrypt failed for profile <id>" — the profile resolves to null, so CMDB endpoints act as if nothing is configured.
• "[ssh-creds] decrypt failed — ignoring env creds" — credentials become {}, so polls are skipped and audits return the no-credentials error.
• Profiles still LIST fine (name, type, Active badge are cleartext) — only the blob fails, so it looks like "the app forgot our password", not an outage.

Causes:
1. .env.key not carried across a redeploy. On next start connection_profiles.loadKey writes a brand-new key and logs "[connection_profiles] generated new encryption key at .env.key" — grep the log for that line, it dates the breakage exactly.
2. SSH_CREDS_KEY set to a different key — the env var wins over the file, so an intact .env.key on disk will not save you.
3. Key file truncated/reformatted — must be exactly 64 hex chars, else the loader throws "<path> must contain a 32-byte hex key (64 chars)".

Recovery: restore the original key (file or env var) from backup BEFORE restarting again, then restart. The blobs are intact; nothing else is needed. If the key is truly lost the secrets are unrecoverable by design — profiles must be re-entered by their owners/org admins in the app, switch credentials re-entered on the server via encrypt-creds.js. Never collect credentials over a support channel.
symptoms: must contain a 32-byte hex key (64 chars)
All connections stopped working after redeploy
Connections still listed but no data pulled
rootCause: Both stores decrypt with a key resolved from SSH_CREDS_KEY or server/.env.key; a missing/replaced key makes decrypt throw, and the code logs and degrades to null/empty credentials rather than failing loudly. connection_profiles.loadKey auto-generates a fresh key when the file is absent, permanently orphaning existing blobs.

question: INTERNAL: is "only admins can manage connections" a real security boundary?
answer:
Partly — and the distinction matters on a security questionnaire.

• Server-enforced: organization-wide credentials. `/api/org-connections/*` is mounted with `requireAuth, requireOrgAdmin` (server/connection_profiles_routes.js:123). requireOrgAdmin 403s anything outside org_admin/owner, 400s if the user has no organization_id, and pins req._orgId; every org query is scoped `WHERE organization_id = ?`.

• NOT server-enforced: the "admins only" part of personal profiles. `/api/connections/*` is mounted with `requireAuth` alone (line 37) — no role check. Any authenticated user, member included, can create/list/update/activate/delete their own profiles via the API. The admin gate is purely client-side: AdminRoute on the /connections route (App.jsx:77-90, 269) plus isAdmin conditionals on the sidebar link (DesktopShell.jsx:197,210) and the Profile page row. UI affordance, not authorization.

• Cross-tenant exposure is real-enforced either way: every personal query filters `WHERE user_id = ?`, so no user can read another's profile or secret.

• No fallback: resolveCredsForType / resolveCredsForOrg return null when there is no matching active profile (connection_profiles.js:347-360, 467-471) — no env or file fallback, so a missing profile degrades to "no data", never to someone else's credentials.

Short version: cross-tenant credential isolation is server-enforced; "only admins can manage connections" is a screen, not a control. A technician can't reach the UI, but nothing in the API stops them storing their own profile.
symptoms: Security review question about connection permissions
Can a member create a connection profile
rootCause: router.use('/api/connections', requireAuth) has no role check and all queries filter by user_id, while /api/org-connections adds requireOrgAdmin; the admin gate on the /connections page comes from AdminRoute and DesktopShell's isAdmin conditional.
